findings.title: [P2] Scan executable expansions inside unquoted heredocs
findings.body:
An unquoted heredoc executes command substitutions, but strip_heredocs removes its entire body before checking for outside paths. For example, `cat <<EOF
$(cat /mnt/private/token)
EOF` reads the external file while check_value sees only `cat <<HEREDOC` and reports no outside_path contamination. This lets an evaluated agent access readable files outside the permitted roots without invalidating its grade. Preserve and scan executable expansions in unquoted heredocs; only treat literal heredoc contents as inert data.

findings.failure_mode: An unquoted heredoc executes command substitutions, but strip_heredocs removes its entire body before checking for outside paths.

findings.description: Grader 1.2.2 strips every heredoc body from a Bash tool_use command before the absolute-path scan (`body = strip_heredocs(val)` at line 1412, then ABS_WORD.finditer(body)). The rationale is that written file text is data, but a heredoc that feeds an interpreter is executed: `bash <<'EOF'\ncat /root/secret\nEOF`, `sh <<EOF`, `python3 - <<EOF ... open('/outside/path')` all reach the filesystem with the paths inside the body. The hidden/suite/repo substring scans still see the full value, but the outside_path check (the only one that detects reading arbitrary files outside the sandbox roots) is blind to the body. The transcript text is produced by the agent under test, which is exactly the party the contamination gate is meant to catch.
findings.failure_mode: An agent run that reads files outside the sandbox through an executed heredoc is graded uncontaminated, so a leaked or out-of-scope result enters runs.jsonl and the ablation report as a valid trial.
findings.suggested_fix: Only strip heredocs whose target command is a known writer (cat > file, tee, cp /dev/stdin); when the word before `<<` is an interpreter (bash, sh, zsh, python*, perl, node, ruby, eval) or unknown, scan the body as well. Alternatively run ABS_WORD on both val and body and union the candidates, dropping only candidates that appear exclusively in a `cat >`/`tee` heredoc.

findings.description: Grader 1.2.5 skips any absolute word whose preceding character is a quote and whose character two back is not whitespace or an operator (line 1442). It does not check that the quote actually closes a string. In bash `""/root/secret` and `''/root/secret` concatenate to `/root/secret`, and `$'/root/secret'` is an ANSI-C quoted literal: in each case body[pos-1] is a quote and body[pos-2] is a quote or `$`, so after_closing_quote returns True and the path is never appended to cands. The multi-component path then escapes outside() entirely.
findings.failure_mode: `cat ""/root/secret`, `cat $'/outside/hidden_tests'` and similar commands read outside the sandbox roots without the trial being marked contaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Require that the quote at pos-1 is a closing quote: scan back from pos-1 to find the matching opening quote and verify a non-empty quoted segment with a non-operator token before it (e.g. `"$D"/x` and `pr/'"$v"'/x`), and reject `$'`, `""` and `''` explicitly. Simpler: only apply the rule when body[pos-2] is an identifier character, `}` or `)`.

findings.failure_mode: Contamination scan stalls; the grade hits LOA_EVAL_GRADE_TIMEOUT_S or the runner watchdog and the trial is rowed infrastructure_error instead of contaminated or scored, so a contaminated or failing run is excluded rather than recorded, and the batch may stall or be marked partial.

findings.description: For Bash commands the case-insensitive substring check (`"hidden" in val.lower()`) is replaced at lines 1394-1396 by HIDDEN_TOKEN = r"HIDDEN|(?<=[/._=-])hidden\b|\bhidden(?=[/_=-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])". This matches only all-caps HIDDEN or lowercase hidden adjacent to / . _ = -. A bare word (`cd hidden; cat *`, `ls hidden`, `cat hidden/*` is caught but `cd hidden` is not) and any mixed case (`Hidden/`, `HiddenTests`) are no longer detected in Bash, while the Read, Grep and Glob paths keep the old any-case substring check. Bash is the tool with the widest reach, so the inconsistency gives the agent a lower bar precisely where it matters.
findings.failure_mode: An agent that changes into a hidden-tests directory with a bare `cd hidden` or uses mixed case is graded uncontaminated and its hidden_tests pass rate is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the case-insensitive check for Bash and instead whitelist the known prose false positive: match `hidden` case-insensitively with re.I and only suppress when the word is inside a stripped heredoc body or is followed by a space-separated English word (e.g. `hidden interaction`). At minimum add re.I to the token regex and a `\bhidden\b` alternative when preceded by cd, ls, cat, find or a path separator.

findings.description: Two smaller gaps in the new skip rules. (a) The one-component skip at lines 1422-1424 interacts with ABS_WORD, whose character class excludes glob and brace characters: `cat /roo?/secret`, `cat /r*/secret` or `cat /ro{o,}t/secret` yield w = `/roo`, `/r` or `/ro`, a single component not in SENSITIVE_SINGLE, so the word is skipped; before 1.2.1 it was a candidate and flagged as outside. (b) in_quotes (lines 1372-1374) counts all quotes in body[:pos] with no escape or pairing logic, so an earlier apostrophe (`echo don't; cat /root/`) flips parity and the sensitive one-component word is skipped at line 1444. Both need the agent to write unusual shell, so impact is limited, but they are cheap to close.
findings.failure_mode: Shell globs or an earlier apostrophe make an outside-root read invisible to the contamination scan.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend ABS_WORD's character class with `?*[]{}` so glob-shaped words keep their full component count, and only apply the one-component skip when the word is followed by whitespace or end of string. Replace in_quotes with a small tokenizer that tracks single and double quoting state and backslash escapes, or restrict the rule to words that sit between a pair of quotes on the same line.
